title: PBMC, placebo, IMH, rep 1
extract_protocol_ch1: Patients with anterior STEMI were precribed either placebo or KAND567 and donated a blood sample 24 hours after treatment. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) were isolated from these samples and frozen at -800C. After thawing, cells were washed, counted and resuspended in PBS supplemented with 0.04% w/v BSA.

The libraries were generated according to the manufacturer’s instructions (User Guide CG000733, Rev A Chromium GEM-X  Single Cell 5' Reagent Kits v3, 10x Genomics). Briefly, barcoded beads, PBMC resuspended in master mix and partitioning oil were combined and loaded onto the GEM-X 5’ chip in order to generate gel bead-in-emulsion (GEMs). The gel bead was then dissolved and any co-partitioned cell was lysed. The cell lysate was incubated with a master mix containing reverse transcription reagents and poly(dT) primers, along with gel bead primers containing Illumina R1 (read 1) sequencing primer, a 10x barcode, a unique molecular identifier and a template switch oligo, which lead to the generation of 10x barcoded first strand cDNA from poly-A RNA. The first strand cDNA from each sample was then purified with silane magnetic beads and full-length cDNA amplified by PCR. Following enzymatic fragmentation, the appropriately sized cDNA amplicons were used to construct the 5’ gene expression library. During library construction, P5, P7, i5 and i7 sample indexes and Illumina R2 (read 2) primer sequence were added, such that the final libraries contained the P5 and P7 primers used in the Illumina amplification.
data_processing: Using 10X Genomics' CellRanger v8.0.1, the raw BCL files from the sequencer were converted to FASTQ format using the mkfastq function.
Again using CellRanger v8.0.1, counts were generated on per sample basis using CellRanger's multi function, outputting a filtered feature count matrix in .h5 format.
Assembly: GRCh38-2024-A
Supplementary files format and content: HDF5 – a binary format storing a barcode matrix for each sample
contact_address: International Centre for Life, Central Parkway
